about: Answer choices for the Question Bank's written-answer questions; written by scripts/question_choices.py.

options: From human reason and personal experience with God in daily life
From the inner light and conscience that God has given to us
From church tradition and the teachings of spiritual leaders throughout history
From the Bible, through which God revealed Himself as the supreme standard for belief and living
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: From the Bible, through which God revealed Himself as the supreme standard for belief and living

options: His body was restored to normal human form and remained on earth
He appeared only as a vision or phantom to His disciples
Raised from the dead with a glorified body and appeared to disciples
His spirit rose to heaven but His body remained in the tomb
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Raised from the dead with a glorified body and appeared to disciples

options: Jesus stayed on earth in His disciples and remains invisible
Jesus ascended into heaven and is now exalted to honor and power
Jesus returned to heaven but remains distant and uninvolved with the world
Jesus is seated at God's right hand but has no power
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Jesus ascended into heaven and is now exalted to honor and power

options: He will return in power and glory to judge the world.
He will come to earth as a humble servant to teach again
He will return invisibly but will not judge anyone
He has already returned in the form of the Holy Spirit
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: He will return in power and glory to judge the world.

options: The Holy Spirit is God's power but not a person or divine being
The Holy Spirit is less divine than God the Father and Son
The Holy Spirit is a created being sent by God to help us
The Holy Spirit is the Spirit of God and is fully divine.
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: The Holy Spirit is the Spirit of God and is fully divine.

options: He came to earth in human form and died for the sins of the world
He comforted disciples and distributed spiritual gifts to church members
He was sent at Pentecost to give believers power to witness
He was involved in creation, inspired holy men to write Scripture, empowered Jesus, and raised Him
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: He was involved in creation, inspired holy men to write Scripture, empowered Jesus, and raised Him

options: Evolved from animals and differ only in degree, not essential nature
Made in God's image but destined to achieve God-like power
In God's image, male and female, with purpose to know and enjoy God
Created as servants of God with no significance or special value
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: In God's image, male and female, with purpose to know and enjoy God

options: God created man both innocent and with a natural inclination to sin
Man was created with knowledge of good and evil and ability to choose
Created innocent with free choice, man sinned, bringing sin and death
God predestined man to sin so that Christ could provide salvation
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Created innocent with free choice, man sinned, bringing sin and death

options: Satan's temptation affected only Adam and Eve, not all people
Man fell through Satan's temptation, so all are born inclined to sin
People sin because they live in a sinful environment, not by nature
Satan caused all humans to sin immediately upon their birth
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Man fell through Satan's temptation, so all are born inclined to sin

options: Sin is only when we intentionally break rules we know about
Only actions that harm others or break human laws constitute sin
Contrary to God's will or not done as faith for God's glory
Thoughts and feelings are not sinful; only deliberate actions are
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Contrary to God's will or not done as faith for God's glory

options: Church councils selected and approved writings that became the Bible we have today
Men inspired by God wrote the Bible, making God its author, without error and totally true
Different men wrote the Bible over centuries with some mistakes but mostly truth
Prophets and apostles wrote the Bible with guidance from church leaders
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Men inspired by God wrote the Bible, making God its author, without error and totally true

options: Yes, we must earn God's love through perfect obedience
God's love only comes to those who truly believe in Him
We must first earn God's love through obedience and good works
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: No! God loved us first.

options: God's holiness hates sin, His justice punishes it, separating us under condemnation
God tolerates sin if we confess it and promise to improve
God's punishment for sin is harsh, but His love prevents Him from enforcing it
Sin harms us but God overlooks it because of His mercy
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: God's holiness hates sin, His justice punishes it, separating us under condemnation

options: Salvation is through baptism and faith in Jesus Christ as Lord
Salvation comes through faith in Christ combined with good works and obedience
Salvation requires faith in Christ plus keeping God's commandments perfectly
Salvation is only through grace of God and personal faith in Jesus Christ
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Salvation is only through grace of God and personal faith in Jesus Christ

options: God's decision to choose those who show faith before the world began
God's eternal choice based on who would believe and do good works
God's plan to save all people equally through preaching the gospel
God's eternal plan, formed before the world began, to save sinners through spreading the Gospel
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: God's eternal plan, formed before the world began, to save sinners through spreading the Gospel

options: In repentance toward God and faith in the Lord Jesus Christ
In confession of sins to a priest and sincere regret
In a public declaration of faith before witnesses
In baptism and joining a local Christian church
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: In repentance toward God and faith in the Lord Jesus Christ

options: Repentance is a sincere change of mind and of attitude in which the sinner turns to God from sin
Repentance is stopping sinful behavior and promising to try harder to be good
Repentance means doing penance for sins to earn God's forgiveness and cleansing
Repentance is feeling sorry for your sins and confessing them to a priest or pastor
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Repentance is a sincere change of mind and of attitude in which the sinner turns to God from sin

options: Believing the right facts about Jesus and understanding the gospel message correctly
Trusting Jesus to forgive you, change your life, and provide you a home in Heaven
Having faith that God exists and trusting he will help you in trouble
Knowing about Jesus and committing to follow his teachings and obey his laws
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Trusting Jesus to forgive you, change your life, and provide you a home in Heaven

options: A spiritual experience where believers receive special power from the Holy Spirit
Being baptized and becoming a member of the church as a believer
New life; being born again; the Holy Spirit makes people alive to God and changes their direction
A process of becoming holy through prayer and keeping God's laws carefully
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: New life; being born again; the Holy Spirit makes people alive to God and changes their direction

options: One of many spiritual beings who rules over the universe
A distant, unknown power that created the world and withdrew
An impersonal force that guides the universe and all creation
The only living and true God, first and best of all beings
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: The only living and true God, first and best of all beings

options: When a person becomes Christian, God makes them part of His eternal family as children of God
When a person is baptized, God officially recognizes them as adopted children
When a person repents of sin, they become God's family and inherit life
When a person joins the church, they are accepted into God's household
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: When a person becomes Christian, God makes them part of His eternal family as children of God

options: Being set apart for God and growing toward spiritual maturity through the Holy Spirit
Becoming free from all sin and living a perfect life that pleases God
Growing in faith and knowledge by studying the Bible and obeying all laws
A process of removing evil desires and becoming completely holy through discipline
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Being set apart for God and growing toward spiritual maturity through the Holy Spirit

options: The Holy Spirit gives believers special abilities and spiritual gifts for God's service
The Holy Spirit fills believers at Pentecost to empower them for witnessing
At salvation the Holy Spirit baptizes believers into Christ's Body and comes to live inside them
After water baptism the Holy Spirit comes to dwell within the believer permanently
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: At salvation the Holy Spirit baptizes believers into Christ's Body and comes to live inside them

options: Being freed from all earthly concerns and dwelling in God's perfect kingdom
God completing salvation: being freed from temptation, made like Jesus, and receiving a glorified body for eternity
Becoming like the angels and receiving a spiritual body for eternal worship
Being rewarded in heaven based on how faithful and good you were on earth
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: God completing salvation: being freed from temptation, made like Jesus, and receiving a glorified body for eternity

options: Real Christians will continue in faith to the end and be kept by God's power for salvation
Once a person is saved, they are guaranteed to go to heaven regardless of behavior
Real Christians must obey God's commands to remain saved until the very end
Christians who stumble into sin can lose their salvation and be lost forever
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Real Christians will continue in faith to the end and be kept by God's power for salvation

options: A local congregation of baptized believers voluntarily joined together in covenant with Christ and each other
Any group of Christians who worship together and fellowship in a community
An organization of baptized believers established by apostles to teach and discipline
A denomination of baptized Christians organized by church leaders to spread the gospel
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: A local congregation of baptized believers voluntarily joined together in covenant with Christ and each other

options: To protect Christian beliefs, preserve traditions, and prepare believers for Christ's return
To teach biblical doctrine, collect offerings, and discipline members who disobey God
To provide social services, comfort the sick, and build community among believers
To glorify God, observe ordinances, spread the gospel, and provide fellowship and accountability
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: To glorify God, observe ordinances, spread the gospel, and provide fellowship and accountability

options: Each congregation follows the leadership of a bishop or denominational headquarters
Church governance is determined by majority vote and the judgment of leaders
Church decisions are made by pastors and elders appointed to govern the congregation
Each congregation operates under Christ's Lordship through democratic processes with Christ as the Head
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Each congregation operates under Christ's Lordship through democratic processes with Christ as the Head

options: God is a spiritual being who exists everywhere and knows all things perfectly
God is Spirit, personal, Creator distinct from creation, perfect, all-powerful and all-knowing
God is powerful, knowing, present everywhere, and perfect in all his qualities
God is an impersonal force that created everything and is beyond understanding
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: God is Spirit, personal, Creator distinct from creation, perfect, all-powerful and all-knowing

options: Pastors, deacons, elders, and bishops appointed by higher authorities
Pastors and deacons; pastor office limited to biblically qualified men
Elders and presbyters selected for life based on age
Pastors and ordained clergy chosen from the most educated members
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Pastors and deacons; pastor office limited to biblically qualified men

options: All churches that share the same theological and denominational beliefs
The leadership of all Christian denominations working together
The Body of Christ including all redeemed of all ages and nations
The Christian churches in a particular city or region
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: The Body of Christ including all redeemed of all ages and nations

options: Believer's baptism: immersion beneath water in the name of the Trinity
Sprinkling water on believers in the name of the Father and the Son
Infant baptism: sprinkling or pouring water on people to cleanse from sin
Pouring water on baptized believers in the name of the Trinity together
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Believer's baptism: immersion beneath water in the name of the Trinity

options: No. Baptism is an optional practice for those who wish to be baptized
No. Baptism is a testimony of salvation but not required for membership
Yes. Being a church ordinance, baptism is required to observe the Lord's Supper and before the privileges of church membership
Yes. Baptism is required for membership, but not required to take communion
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Yes. Being a church ordinance, baptism is required to observe the Lord's Supper and before the privileges of church membership

options: Baptism saves people from their sins and makes them part of church
Baptism testifies that a person is already saved; it represents the Spirit's inward baptism bringing us into God's family
Baptism is a requirement for salvation that demonstrates your commitment to Jesus
Baptism is an act that brings salvation to the person being baptized
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Baptism testifies that a person is already saved; it represents the Spirit's inward baptism bringing us into God's family

options: The believer's baptism in water and receiving the Holy Spirit's power
Jesus' death and resurrection; believer's death to old life and raising to new life in Christ
Jesus' payment for sin and the believer's promise to obey God always
Jesus' sacrifice for our sins and the believer's commitment to follow him
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Jesus' death and resurrection; believer's death to old life and raising to new life in Christ

options: A ritual of sharing a meal to remember Jesus and await his return
A religious ceremony where believers eat bread and wine as a sacrifice
The Lord's Supper: a symbolic act of eating bread and drinking cup, remembering Christ's death
A practice of communion with Christ through eating bread and wine together
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: The Lord's Supper: a symbolic act of eating bread and drinking cup, remembering Christ's death

options: Sunday is the Christian day of rest to honor God and family
The Lord's Day is Saturday, when God rested after creating the world
The Lord's Day is a holy day set apart from worldly pleasures
Sunday, first day celebrating Christ's resurrection; a day for God, fellowship, worship, and pleasing activities
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Sunday, first day celebrating Christ's resurrection; a day for God, fellowship, worship, and pleasing activities

options: The kingdom of God is a future state of eternal peace in heaven
God's rule over all things; God ruling in believers' hearts now; to be completed when Jesus returns
God's rule over creation that existed before time and will end with Christ
God's kingdom is the church where believers gather to worship and serve
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: God's rule over all things; God ruling in believers' hearts now; to be completed when Jesus returns

options: Jesus will come again invisibly to remove believers before the final judgment
Jesus will return spiritually to believers' hearts and usher in new creation
Jesus will return to establish God's kingdom and bring peace on earth
Jesus will return personally and visibly in glory, raise the dead, and judge all people
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Jesus will return personally and visibly in glory, raise the dead, and judge all people

options: God is one person who took on three different roles at different times
God is three separate Gods united in purpose and agreement together
Three Persons—Father, Son, Spirit—each fully God, not one-third; there is only one God
God manifests himself as three powers but is essentially one force
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Three Persons—Father, Son, Spirit—each fully God, not one-third; there is only one God

options: Heaven is God's throne room and a place of eternal reward and joy
It is the place from which God reigns over the universe. It is a perfect place without sin or suffering
Heaven is the realm of God where no sin exists and all worship
Heaven is a perfect place where believers are rewarded for their faithful works
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: It is the place from which God reigns over the universe. It is a perfect place without sin or suffering

options: To win the lost by telling about Jesus and Christian example; every Christian should make disciples
To live a moral life and hope others will ask about your faith
To teach biblical truth and encourage people to join the church fellowship
To spread the gospel through the church and support missionary organizations worldwide
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: To win the lost by telling about Jesus and Christian example; every Christian should make disciples

options: Traveling to other countries to convert people to the Christian faith
International mission work through sending missionaries to other countries for service
Preaching the gospel to unreached people groups in foreign lands and places
Evangelism to people of other cultures and languages; preaching the gospel to all nations
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Evangelism to people of other cultures and languages; preaching the gospel to all nations

options: Dedicating your life and resources to God's kingdom work and missions
Using your abilities and wealth to help the poor and needy in need
Managing God's resources—time, talents, possessions, Gospel—the way God wants
Giving money to the church and serving in church organizations and ministries
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Managing God's resources—time, talents, possessions, Gospel—the way God wants

options: Christians should tithe ten percent of their income to their local church
Christians give offerings to the Lord's work when they feel led by Spirit
Christians should give generously, regularly, with joy to support God's kingdom work
Christians should give to the Lord's work cheerfully, regularly, and generously. The more they make the more they should give
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Christians should give to the Lord's work cheerfully, regularly, and generously. The more they make the more they should give

options: God's creation; one man and one woman in lifetime covenant; children are a blessing
God's plan for couples to live together, have children, and build community
A social institution of one man and one woman with shared responsibilities
God's creation; two people united in love and commitment for life together
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: God's creation; one man and one woman in lifetime covenant; children are a blessing

options: Parents teach and guide children while children learn to be responsible people
Parents exemplify God's plan, teach about God and values, discipline lovingly; children honor parents and learn biblical wisdom
Parents provide discipline and instruction; children should obey and learn obedience
Parents should train and discipline children, while children obey and respect parents
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Parents exemplify God's plan, teach about God and values, discipline lovingly; children honor parents and learn biblical wisdom

options: Yes, Baptists are the true church; we don't work with other denominations
No, but Baptist teachings best match the Bible; we work with others
No; salvation is through Jesus, not denomination; we cooperate with other Christians on mutual concerns
No, many churches lead to salvation; we partner with other Christian groups
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: No; salvation is through Jesus, not denomination; we cooperate with other Christians on mutual concerns

options: God rules the universe through secondary causes and natural laws alone
God is the Creator, Redeemer, Preserver, and Ruler of the universe.
God created the universe but is no longer involved with it
God preserves creation but other beings share in ruling it
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: God is the Creator, Redeemer, Preserver, and Ruler of the universe.

options: Yes, but personal experience is more important than doctrine and theology
Maybe, as long as people sincerely follow their own understanding of God
Yes; the Bible commands sound doctrine; right thinking leads to right living
No, what matters is personal faith and living a good moral life
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Yes; the Bible commands sound doctrine; right thinking leads to right living

options: Son of God, born of virgin Mary, who was fully human deity
Jesus was God's adopted Son, born of Mary, who became divine being
Eternal Son of God, conceived by Holy Spirit, born of Mary, fully God and human
Eternal God who became human through Mary's womb for our salvation
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Eternal Son of God, conceived by Holy Spirit, born of Mary, fully God and human

options: He perfectly kept God's law except when it interfered with his mission
He lived a good life by human standards but had some failures
He kept the ceremonial law but broke the moral law for others
He obeyed all God's commandments and perfectly followed God's will
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: He obeyed all God's commandments and perfectly followed God's will

options: To teach us how to live by His example and moral teaching
Die on the cross as a substitute for our sins, securing forgiveness
To demonstrate God's love but not to actually pay for our sins
To show us how to overcome sin through our own effort and will
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Die on the cross as a substitute for our sins, securing forgiveness

options: God is the Supreme Being worthy of all worship and praise
God is the eternal Creator of all that exists
God is the First and Chiefest Being
God is the most powerful and wisest of all beings
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: God is the First and Chiefest Being

options: God's purpose to create the world and establish his kingdom eternally
God's Eternal Purpose according to the Counsel of his Will, whereby he foreordained whatsoever comes to pass
God's plan to save his chosen people according to his perfect will
God's eternal decisions about what will happen in the universe forever
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: God's Eternal Purpose according to the Counsel of his Will, whereby he foreordained whatsoever comes to pass

options: By dipping only part of the body in water according to church practice.
By dipping in water but without regard to the name of Trinity.
By immersion or dipping the whole body in water according to Christ's institution.
By sprinkling or pouring water on the head according to church tradition.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: By immersion or dipping the whole body in water according to Christ's institution.

options: To join the most popular and culturally dominant church regardless of theology.
To remain independent and not commit to any church in their practice.
To give themselves to a particular orderly church and walk in commandments.
To participate in all churches equally without particular commitment to one fellowship.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: To give themselves to a particular orderly church and walk in commandments.

options: Examine themselves for knowledge to discern the Lord's body and faith.
Examine themselves only for past sins without considering present faith and obedience.
Partake freely without any examination or requirement of repentance and obedience.
Come to the Lord's Supper without self-examination, trusting in church membership alone.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Examine themselves for knowledge to discern the Lord's body and faith.

options: Addressing God directly without the assistance of the Holy Spirit or Christ.
Offering our desires to God by the Spirit for things agreeable to his will.
Reciting prescribed formulas without genuine desire, confession, or thankfulness toward God.
Requesting whatever we want from God without regard for his will.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Offering our desires to God by the Spirit for things agreeable to his will.

options: The traditions of the church and the writings of church fathers guide prayer.
The whole Word of God directs us in prayer; especially the Lord's Prayer.
Personal feelings and individual preferences guide prayer more than Scripture or teaching.
Only the Psalms provide proper direction for what and how to pray.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The whole Word of God directs us in prayer; especially the Lord's Prayer.

options: To approach God with Reverence and Confidence as Children to a Father, and to pray with and for others
That we approach God with proper fear and intercede for people
That we should pray privately for ourselves and trust God completely
To speak to God respectfully and reverently with humility before him
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: To approach God with Reverence and Confidence as Children to a Father, and to pray with and for others

options: That God would be honored and all creation would praise him
That God would enable us to glorify his Name in all whereby he maketh himself known and dispose all things to his Glory
That we would make God's name known and fulfill his purpose
That God's name would be holy and we would live righteously
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: That God would enable us to glorify his Name in all whereby he maketh himself known and dispose all things to his Glory

options: That God's physical kingdom be established on earth with political power.
That our own personal wealth and power increase in this world.
That Satan's kingdom be destroyed and the kingdom of grace be advanced.
That the church become the dominant institution in all nations and cultures.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: That Satan's kingdom be destroyed and the kingdom of grace be advanced.

options: That God's will on earth mirror human preferences rather than heaven's order.
That God by his grace makes us willing to know and obey his will.
That God's will be forcibly imposed on the earth through human power.
That we be exempted from God's will if it conflicts with desires.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: That God by his grace makes us willing to know and obey his will.

options: Teaches us to take encouragement from God alone and to praise him.
Teaches to distribute praise between God and other spiritual beings or forces.
The conclusion emphasizes human worthiness and merit as basis for God hearing.
Indicates doubt whether God will hear us and advises trying multiple prayers.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Teaches us to take encouragement from God alone and to praise him.

options: It is reasonable to believe in God, though some may doubt his existence
Those who don't believe in God are foolish and destined for punishment
Every One ought to believe there is a God; and it is their great Sin and Folly who do not
Everyone should try to believe in God, but faith is a personal choice
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Every One ought to believe there is a God; and it is their great Sin and Folly who do not

options: Satan's power, human weakness, ignorance of God's law, and worldly pride
Guilt of Adam's Sin, want of Original Righteousness, Corruption of Nature, and all actual Transgressions
Serpent's deception, Eve's weakness, lack of knowledge, and disobedience to God
The forbidden fruit, the garden's curse, Adam's shame, and all mortal suffering
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Guilt of Adam's Sin, want of Original Righteousness, Corruption of Nature, and all actual Transgressions

options: By their Fall, Mankind lost Communion with God, are under his Wrath and Curse, liable to Death and Pains of Hell forever
By eating the fruit, Mankind lost innocence, faced God's anger, were exiled, and must suffer
By their Fall, Mankind lost the Garden, gained shame, became mortal, and need mercy
By their Disobedience, Mankind lost God's favor, face eternal judgment, earthly struggles, and separation
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: By their Fall, Mankind lost Communion with God, are under his Wrath and Curse, liable to Death and Pains of Hell forever

options: God chose his people for earthly blessing, promised Christ's birth, and made the Law to guide them
God elects believers upon their faith, makes a new covenant, and offers them eternal peace
God provides grace for all mankind, establishes the church, and offers salvation to the obedient
God from all Eternity elected some to Everlasting Life and made a Covenant of Grace to deliver them from Sin and Misery by a Redeemer
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: God from all Eternity elected some to Everlasting Life and made a Covenant of Grace to deliver them from Sin and Misery by a Redeemer

options: Jesus Christ, the greatest of God's prophets, who combined divine wisdom with human nature perfectly
The Lord Jesus Christ, the Eternal Son of God who became Man, being God and Man in two distinct Natures and one Person forever
The Lord Jesus Christ, God's chosen prophet, who was born of Mary and ascended to heaven
The Son of God, who existed in heaven, came to earth as an angel, and died for sins
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The Lord Jesus Christ, the Eternal Son of God who became Man, being God and Man in two distinct Natures and one Person forever

options: The offices of Apostle, High Priest, and Lord both on earth and in heaven
The roles of Teacher, Mediator, and Judge during his life and after his resurrection
The positions of Prophet, Shepherd, and Savior in his suffering and glory
The Offices of a Prophet, of a Priest, and of a King, both in Humiliation and Exaltation
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The Offices of a Prophet, of a Priest, and of a King, both in Humiliation and Exaltation

options: In revealing to us, by his Word and Spirit, the Will of God for our Salvation
In revealing all the Mysteries of God to us through his Spirit alone
By his Word alone, revealing all that God requires of Man in obedience
In teaching us the Law and the consequences of breaking God's Commandments
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: In revealing to us, by his Word and Spirit, the Will of God for our Salvation

options: In his continual Intercession for us and in revealing God's Will for salvation
In offering the sacrifices of the Temple on our behalf to God
In satisfying God's Justice through our repentance and continual Intercession for ourselves
In his once offering of himself a Sacrifice to satisfy Divine Justice, and making continual Intercession
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: In his once offering of himself a Sacrifice to satisfy Divine Justice, and making continual Intercession

options: In defending us from all Trials and establishing an earthly Kingdom for us

In subduing our Enemies through revealing God's Will and making us obedient to him
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: In subduing us to himself, ruling and defending us, and conquering all his and our Enemies

options: The heavens declare God's glory, but the Law teaches his nature and demands obedience
Nature proves there is a God, but the Gospel alone brings knowledge of salvation
The Light of Nature and God's Works declare there is a God; but his Word and Spirit do it fully and effectually for Salvation
Reason and creation show God exists; but only Scripture reveals his character and will
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The Light of Nature and God's Works declare there is a God; but his Word and Spirit do it fully and effectually for Salvation

options: His exercise of prophetic, priestly, and kingly offices with power over all things in heaven and on earth.
His resurrection in glory, His ascension to heaven, and His sitting at the right hand of God the Father.
Born in low condition, made under the Law, undergoing the wrath of God, the cursed death of the Cross, and burial.
His perfect obedience to the Law, His active and passive righteousness, and the satisfaction of God's justice.

options: His resurrection in power, entrance to heaven, return in clouds, and eternal reign over all
His victory over death, placement in glory, advocacy for us, and future judgment of nations
His triumph over Satan, glorification in heaven, intercession for believers, and final return
His rising from the Dead on the third Day, ascending into Heaven, sitting at God's right Hand, and coming to judge the World
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: His rising from the Dead on the third Day, ascending into Heaven, sitting at God's right Hand, and coming to judge the World

options: By giving us the gift of saving faith and making us Children of God
By working Faith in us and thereby uniting us to Christ in our effectual Calling
By making us righteous and enabling us to obey his Law through the Spirit
By revealing Christ to us through his Word and sanctifying our hearts

options: God's grace making us aware of law, showing Christ's love, and transforming our desires
The Spirit's calling of sinners, revealing Christ's power, and strengthening our resolve to obey
God's work giving us faith, teaching us Scripture, and enabling us to live righteously

options: God's free Grace pardoning all our sins and accepting us as Righteous through Christ's imputed Righteousness, received by Faith alone.
God accepting us on the basis of our sincere repentance and our works of obedience to the Law.
Christ living a perfect life as our example, so we might follow His pattern and attain righteousness through imitation.
God making us inwardly holy and renewed through the transforming work of the Holy Spirit in progressive sanctification.

options: The Spirit's action renewing our minds, freeing from sin's power, and empowering obedience
God's process of forgiving us, changing our hearts, freeing us from guilt and shame
The Work of God's Grace whereby we are renewed after God's Image, dying to Sin, living unto Righteousness
God's work making us holy, separating us from worldliness, and perfecting our nature entirely

options: The Holy Scriptures are the Word of God and the only certain Rule of Faith and Obedience
Scripture is the Word of God, and the Church interprets it for us
The Scriptures contain the Word of God and are our guide for living
The Old and New Testaments, along with Church Tradition, are the Rule of Faith
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The Holy Scriptures are the Word of God and the only certain Rule of Faith and Obedience

options: The saved shall be raised immortal, vindicated before all, granted peace, and united with God
Believers shall be transformed gloriously, declared righteous, given crowns, and dwell with Christ eternally
The righteous shall rise in splendor, be rewarded openly, receive eternal honor, and know God
Believers shall be raised up in Glory, openly acknowledged, acquitted at the Day of Judgment, and made perfectly blessed in Soul and Body in God
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Believers shall be raised up in Glory, openly acknowledged, acquitted at the Day of Judgment, and made perfectly blessed in Soul and Body in God

options: The ungodly shall be raised, condemned eternally, tormented by God's justice, and banished forever
The wicked shall perish, be separated from God, suffer separation from life, and face darkness
The lost shall be resurrected, judged guilty, cast into fire with demons, and destroyed eternally
The Bodies of the Wicked shall be raised, sentenced with their Souls to unspeakable Torments with the Devil and his Angels forever
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The Bodies of the Wicked shall be raised, sentenced with their Souls to unspeakable Torments with the Devil and his Angels forever

options: To honor God with all your being, keep his will, and help others as yourself
To obey God's commands with full devotion, honor his name, and serve others faithfully
To worship God completely, keep his law, and treat your neighbor with kindness and justice
To love the Lord our God with all our Heart, Soul, Strength, and Mind, and our Neighbour as ourselves
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: To love the Lord our God with all our Heart, Soul, Strength, and Mind, and our Neighbour as ourselves

options: I am your God who gave you the Law at Mount Sinai
I am the Lord your God who will bring you to the Promised Land
I am the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who brought you through the Wilderness

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of Egypt, out of Bondage

options: The LORD made covenant, provides grace, and rules all things, so we owe him obedience

Because God created us, saved us, and demands obedience, we must follow his law

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Because God is the LORD, our God, and Redeemer, therefore we are bound to keep all his Commandments

options: All Men are not only permitted, but commanded and exhorted, to read, hear, and understand the Holy Scriptures
All Men should read Scripture, but only pastors are commanded to understand it fully
All People are invited to hear God's Word read, but only the learned should interpret it
All believers are encouraged to study Scripture as a means of growing in faith and knowledge
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: All Men are not only permitted, but commanded and exhorted, to read, hear, and understand the Holy Scriptures

options: To believe that God exists and to pray and read Scripture daily
To choose God as our personal Savior and commit our lives to serving him
To know and acknowledge God as the only true God, and to worship and glorify him
To honor God above all things and to obey all his Commandments
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: To know and acknowledge God as the only true God, and to worship and glorify him

options: Requires honoring God alone, forbids denying his existence, and demands true faith always
Forbiddeth rejecting God's authority, serving other powers, and disrespecting his holy name
Forbiddeth denying or not worshipping the true God, and giving his worship and glory to another.
Forbiddeth taking God's name in vain, creating idols, and worshipping false gods instead
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Forbiddeth denying or not worshipping the true God, and giving his worship and glory to another.

options: Thou shalt not worship idols, nor create representations of God, nor pray to statues
Thou shalt not carve false gods, nor make altars to other powers, nor honor them
Thou shalt not build shrines to images, nor bow before them, nor offer them sacrifice
Thou shalt not make graven images or likenesses, nor bow down to them nor serve them.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Thou shalt not make graven images or likenesses, nor bow down to them nor serve them.

options: The receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire all such religious Worship and Ordinances as God appointed
The performing of all religious duties, maintaining God's worship, and following scriptural ordinances
Following God's prescribed forms of worship, maintaining purity in religious practice and ordinances
Accepting and preserving all religious worship, ceremonies, and practices that the church ordained
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire all such religious Worship and Ordinances as God appointed

The making of images of God or the use of images in any worship
The breaking of idols and the refusal to worship any images at all

options: The LORD's power and dominion, his ownership of creation, and his jealousy for purity

God's Sovereignty over us, his Propriety in us, and the Zeal he hath to his own Worship
God's rule over us, his possession of our souls, and his care for true religion
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: God's Sovereignty over us, his Propriety in us, and the Zeal he hath to his own Worship

options: Requires respectful speech about God, honoring his law, and keeping his commandments strictly
Requireth holy and reverent use of God's names, titles, attributes, ordinances, word, and works.
Requireth treating God's name with respect, obeying his word, and worshipping sincerely
Demandeth reverence in prayer, proper use of God's ordinances, and obedience to his teaching

options: What God is like and how we should worship him and serve others
How God created the world and the complete history of mankind from the beginning
The revelation of God, his Character, and all the Laws he demands of us
What Man ought to believe concerning God, and what Duty God requireth of Man
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: What Man ought to believe concerning God, and what Duty God requireth of Man

options: Requireth holy and reverent use of God's names, titles, attributes, and ordinances.
Forbiddeth making and worshipping of graven images and idols.
Forbiddeth the profaning and abusing of any thing whereby God makes himself known.
Forbiddeth denying the true God and giving his worship to another.

options: Breakers may escape Men's Punishment, but the Lord will not suffer them to escape his Righteous Judgment

Transgressors may face earthly consequences, but God's judgment is certain and eternal for all

options: Forbiddeth the making and worshipping of graven images and likenesses.

options: Requireth holy and reverent use of God's names, titles, attributes, and ordinances.

options: A Reward of health and blessing in the land to all who honor their parents
That God will grant length of days and success in life to the obedient
A Promise of long Life and Prosperity (as far as it serves God's Glory) to all who keep it
A Promise of earthly wealth and security to those who obey their parents faithfully

To preserve life at all costs and to avoid all violence and conflict

Forbiddeth all profaning and abusing of any thing whereby God makes himself known.
Forbiddeth all unchaste thoughts, words and actions of any kind whatsoever.

Forbiddeth all unchaste thoughts, words and actions of any manner whatsoever.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Requireth preservation of our own and our neighbor's chastity in heart and behaviour.

The seventh Commandment forbiddeth all unchast Thoughts, Words and Actions.
Forbiddeth taking away of our own or our neighbor's life unjustly.

The stealing of property and the deliberate harm of someone's financial well-being

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Thou shalt not bear false Witness against thy Neighbour

options: Requireth maintaining truth between man and man and of our neighbor's good name.
Requireth lawful procuring and furthering the wealth and outward estate of others.
Forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to truth or injurious to neighbor's good name.
Requireth full contentment with our own condition and charitable frame toward neighbor.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Requireth maintaining truth between man and man and of our neighbor's good name.

options: Forbiddeth discontentment with our own estate or envying the good of neighbor.

Requireth preservation of our own and our neighbor's chastity in all ways.

options: Believers in Christ are able to perfectly keep God's commandments in this life.

Death in this life and eternal separation from God's Love and mercy
Punishment from God now and condemnation at the Day of Judgment

Mere intellectual knowledge of God without faith in Christ or actual repentance.
Works and good deeds alone, without faith in Christ or repentance required.

Mere emotional sorrow for sin without true turning and purpose for obedience.

options: His ordinances especially the Word, Baptism, the Lord's Supper, and Prayer.

All acts of piety that Christians perform without specific ordinance or institution.
The preaching of the gospel only, to the exclusion of all sacraments.

The Spirit blesses the reading of Scripture, making it powerful for faith and holiness
The Holy Spirit uses Scripture reading and preaching to save and build up believers
God's Word preached by his Spirit works to enlighten minds and transform hearts unto God

Through human effort and obedience without need for Christ's blessing or Spirit.

options: To all infants and children of believing parents, whether they profess faith.

options: To refrain from stealing others' property

Two.

To perfect your own holiness and righteousness

options: Yes, when government demands or necessity requires to maintain truth, promote fidelity for God's glory and neighbour's good; saints did rightly.

Show honor and obedience only to parents, not others
