Our death is not payment for our sins but ends sin and enters eternal life
Our death is suffering required for Christ's sake
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Our death is not payment for our sins but ends sin and enters eternal life

options: Through Christ's death our old nature is crucified with Him so we may offer ourselves as a sacrifice to Him
Through Christ's death our sinful desires are permanently removed
Through Christ's death we receive power over temptation
Through Christ's death our nature is made perfectly holy
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Through Christ's death our old nature is crucified with Him so we may offer ourselves as a sacrifice to Him

options: By His resurrection Christ opened heaven to all believers
By His resurrection Christ proved He was God's Son
By His resurrection Christ overcame death, shares righteousness with us, raises us to new life, and pledges our glorious resurrection
By His resurrection Christ defeated Satan and restored paradise
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: By His resurrection Christ overcame death, shares righteousness with us, raises us to new life, and pledges our glorious resurrection

options: His divinity and humanity are completely separate natures not truly united in one person.
His divinity has no limits, is present everywhere, and is personally united with His human nature.
His human nature became unlimited and present everywhere after His ascension to heaven.
His divine nature alone is truly present everywhere; His human nature exists nowhere.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: His divinity has no limits, is present everywhere, and is personally united with His human nature.

options: Our Judge in heaven who examines and pronounces judgment
Our Intercessor in heaven who forgives sins and grants grace
Our Mediator in heaven who transfers our prayers above
Our Advocate in heaven; our flesh there pledges He will take us; Spirit sent enables us to seek heavenly things.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Our Advocate in heaven; our flesh there pledges He will take us; Spirit sent enables us to seek heavenly things.

options: By His Spirit He reveals truth; by power judges evil
By His Spirit He pours out heavenly gifts; by His power He defends us against all enemies.
By His Spirit He enables good works; by power judges
By His Spirit He comforts us; by power judges sin
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: By His Spirit He pours out heavenly gifts; by His power He defends us against all enemies.

options: He is God's gift to believers for moral perfection
He is true eternal God with Father and Son; given to share Christ with me, comfort me, and remain forever.
He is the presence of God in all creation
He is the power of God from Father and Son
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: He is true eternal God with Father and Son; given to share Christ with me, comfort me, and remain forever.

options: Christ's church includes all nations and religions serving
Christ established the church through apostles as its leaders
Christ gathers the church from all time through His Spirit and Word in true faith, and I'm a living member.
The church consists of all good people everywhere
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Christ gathers the church from all time through His Spirit and Word in true faith, and I'm a living member.

options: Believers possess blessings and must advance church mission
Believers receive gifts for their own spiritual growth
Believers inherit Christ's righteousness and must evangelize
Believers as Christ's members share in His treasures and gifts; everyone must use their gifts for others' benefit.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Believers as Christ's members share in His treasures and gifts; everyone must use their gifts for others' benefit.

options: God will remember my sins but mercifully reduce punishment
God will forgive my sins if I repent sincerely
God won't remember my sins or sinful nature against me but grants me Christ's righteousness so I never face condemnation.
God will not punish me if I obey faithfully
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: God won't remember my sins or sinful nature against me but grants me Christ's righteousness so I never face condemnation.

options: Soul goes to Christ; flesh is raised by His power, reunited with soul, made like His glorious body.
My soul goes to heaven but my body remains sleeping in the earth eternally.
I will exist forever as a spirit in heaven completely without any body.
My body is raised purely spiritual and invisible, with no physical substance whatsoever.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Soul goes to Christ; flesh is raised by His power, reunited with soul, made like His glorious body.

options: I will know eternal rest where I cease pain
I will experience endless happiness in God's presence
I will enjoy perfect rest and peace permanently
I already feel eternal joy's beginning in my heart; I will possess perfect blessedness beyond perception and praise God forever.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: I already feel eternal joy's beginning in my heart; I will possess perfect blessedness beyond perception and praise God forever.

options: No. God created man good and in His image in righteousness and holiness to know Him eternally
No. God created man with free will to choose
No. God created man as a servant to obey
No. God created man innocent but not in His image
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. God created man good and in His image in righteousness and holiness to know Him eternally

options: Only by faith in Christ joined with repentance always
Only by faith in Christ and by my good works
Only by faith in Christ, the example of righteousness
Only by faith in Christ; God imputes Christ's satisfaction and righteousness to me as though I never sinned and fully obeyed.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Only by faith in Christ; God imputes Christ's satisfaction and righteousness to me as though I never sinned and fully obeyed.

options: Not by works of the law but by faith
Not through my effort but through God's grace working
Not through church or sacraments but through personal faith
Not because faith itself is righteous, but Christ's satisfaction and righteousness is my righteousness; I receive it by faith only.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Not because faith itself is righteous, but Christ's satisfaction and righteousness is my righteousness; I receive it by faith only.

options: Holy visible signs and seals instituted by God declaring and sealing forgiveness and eternal life through Christ's one sacrifice.
Holy rites by which God works grace into souls
Holy ceremonies commanded by God through church to sanctify
Holy ordinances showing our commitment to Christ and church
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Holy visible signs and seals instituted by God declaring and sealing forgiveness and eternal life through Christ's one sacrifice.

options: Yes, but sacraments and works together complete salvation
Yes, the Holy Spirit teaches in gospel and assures by sacraments that our entire salvation rests on Christ's one sacrifice.
Yes, though sacraments are less important than experience
Yes, but sacraments must be added to faith
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Yes, the Holy Spirit teaches in gospel and assures by sacraments that our entire salvation rests on Christ's one sacrifice.

options: Seven: baptism, confirmation, penance, eucharist, unction, orders, and matrimony.
Three: baptism, the supper, and confirmation as practiced in the church.
Two: holy baptism and the holy supper.
One: only baptism, as the supper is merely a memorial meal.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Two: holy baptism and the holy supper.

options: Baptism removes original sin and opens spiritual rebirth
Baptism imparts God's grace and forgives all transgressions
Water in baptism washes dirt as His blood and Spirit wash away all my sins, Christ's promise at His institution.
Baptism symbolizes our commitment to follow Christ faithfully
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Water in baptism washes dirt as His blood and Spirit wash away all my sins, Christ's promise at His institution.

options: From God's strict law which condemns and drives
From the serpent's deception which continues tempting us
From the fall and disobedience of Adam and Eve, by which our nature became corrupt and sinful
From our own personal choices and failures as adults
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: From the fall and disobedience of Adam and Eve, by which our nature became corrupt and sinful

options: God intends baptism to symbolize while Spirit cleanses
God says baptism actually removes sins and guarantees redemption
God teaches blood and Spirit remove sins like water removes dirt, and assures us we're truly cleansed spiritually as bodily.
God wants us to understand baptism's power mysteriously
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: God teaches blood and Spirit remove sins like water removes dirt, and assures us we're truly cleansed spiritually as bodily.

options: Yes, to dedicate them to God and church
Yes, infants belong to God's covenant and receive redemption and Spirit; baptism grafts them into the church replacing circumcision.
Yes, because they are born into Christian families
No, only believing professed faith should be baptized
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Yes, infants belong to God's covenant and receive redemption and Spirit; baptism grafts them into the church replacing circumcision.

options: The bread and wine mysteriously become His body blood
Commands remembrance through eating bread and drinking cup; His body and blood nourish my soul as surely as I receive these signs.
His actual body and blood are present in bread
He is spiritually present when believers receive with faith
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Commands remembrance through eating bread and drinking cup; His body and blood nourish my soul as surely as I receive these signs.

options: No. The bread and wine symbolize body and blood
No. Bread and wine represent body and blood symbolically
No. Water isn't changed to blood in baptism; bread isn't changed to body in supper but is called so sacramentally.
No. The elements remain unchanged but convey grace
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. Water isn't changed to blood in baptism; bread isn't changed to body in supper but is called so sacramentally.

options: The bread and wine are merely symbols of Christ's body and blood with no real spiritual significance to believers
The bread and wine physically transform into His body and blood through the priest's consecration for literal consumption
Through priestly blessing, Christ's body is daily re-offered for the sins of both living and dead
Bread nourishes bodies as His body nourishes souls eternally; by Spirit we truly share in Him and His suffering becomes ours.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Bread nourishes bodies as His body nourishes souls eternally; by Spirit we truly share in Him and His suffering becomes ours.

options: Yes, unless we are regenerated by the Spirit of God.
No, we can do some good works through natural strength
Yes, but we can gradually improve ourselves through moral effort
Yes, but God will eventually forgive even such corruption through grace
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Yes, unless we are regenerated by the Spirit of God.

options: The mass teaches that complete forgiveness comes only through daily priest-offered sacrifice, not through Christ's one historical death
The Lord's Supper and the mass are essentially the same, both offering Christ's sacrifice daily for the living and dead
Supper witnesses complete forgiveness through Christ's one sacrifice; mass wrongly teaches daily re-offering and worship of Christ bodily present in bread.
Both Supper and mass teach that Christ is present in the bread and wine to be worshipped by believers
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Supper witnesses complete forgiveness through Christ's one sacrifice; mass wrongly teaches daily re-offering and worship of Christ bodily present in bread.

options: All professing Christians should come to the table to participate in Christ's ongoing sacrifice for the forgiveness of sins
Those displeased with sins yet trusting in their forgiveness, covered by Christ, desiring to strengthen faith and amend life. Hypocrites and unrepentant eat judgment.
Only those who are perfect in their faith and have completely stopped sinning are permitted to come to the table
All who believe in Christ may come, for they are automatically cleansed of all sins by faith alone unconditionally
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Those displeased with sins yet trusting in their forgiveness, covered by Christ, desiring to strengthen faith and amend life. Hypocrites and unrepentant eat judgment.

options: The authority of priests alone to forgive sins and administer the sacraments to cleanse the congregation
The apostle Peter alone, to whom Christ gave the exclusive keys to bind and loose all sins eternally
Gospel preaching and church discipline. These open the kingdom to believers and close it to unbelievers.
Prayer and fasting by the church leaders, by which the kingdom is spiritually opened to the worthy
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Gospel preaching and church discipline. These open the kingdom to believers and close it to unbelievers.

options: Gospel opens the kingdom by proclaiming God's forgiveness to believers; closes it by proclaiming His wrath on unbelievers who don't repent.
The gospel declares that believers receive automatic forgiveness without repentance, while unbelievers face eternal separation from God's presence
The gospel proclaims forgiveness to all people indiscriminately, promising that God's love prevents any from experiencing His eternal wrath
Gospel preaching by the church opens the kingdom only to those who receive the sacraments from authorized priests
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Gospel opens the kingdom by proclaiming God's forgiveness to believers; closes it by proclaiming His wrath on unbelievers who don't repent.

options: Church discipline immediately excommunicates those who sin without any chance for repentance or restoration to the church community
Members showing unchristian behavior should be privately criticized by elders but allowed to continue receiving all church sacraments
Unchristian members are admonished, reported to elders, forbidden sacraments, and excluded. They're received back when they show real amendment.
Sinful church members are permanently barred from the church once admonished, never permitted to return regardless of their later repentance
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Unchristian members are admonished, reported to elders, forbidden sacraments, and excluded. They're received back when they show real amendment.

options: We do good works because Christ's redemption obligates us to keep God's law perfectly to maintain our salvation
Show thankfulness to God and praise Him; assure ourselves of faith by its fruits; win neighbors to Christ by godly living.
Good works are necessary to earn God's favor, since our justification depends on the quality of our righteous deeds
Good works are optional displays of superior piety for Christians, but are not required by God for any believer
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Show thankfulness to God and praise Him; assure ourselves of faith by its fruits; win neighbors to Christ by godly living.

options: Repentance is making satisfaction and payment to God for our sinful acts.
Repentance is obeying God's law perfectly for the rest of our life on earth.
It is the dying of the old nature and the coming to life of the new.
Repentance is feeling deep remorse and sorrow for the sins we have committed.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: It is the dying of the old nature and the coming to life of the new.

options: To feel deep regret for the consequences of sin but without necessarily rejecting sin itself as offensive to God
To grieve with heartfelt sorrow that we offended God by sin, and increasingly to hate and flee from it.
To recognize that sinning is wrong in theory while continuing to practice sin with an understanding that grace covers it
To temporarily mourn one's sins while aware they will be forgiven, and then gradually to move beyond the grief
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: To grieve with heartfelt sorrow that we offended God by sin, and increasingly to hate and flee from it.

options: No. God created man able to obey. Man's disobedience robbed all descendants of these gifts
No, humans still retain the ability to perfectly obey God's law despite the fall if they try very hard
Yes, God's law is unjust because He requires what humans cannot naturally accomplish without divine grace assistance always
No, God created all people with enough power to obey if they educate themselves in God's moral law
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. God created man able to obey. Man's disobedience robbed all descendants of these gifts

options: The determination to obey God's law through human effort and willpower, demonstrating one's superior righteousness compared to others
The feeling of satisfaction that comes from successfully performing good works and receiving praise from Christian community members
Heartfelt joy in God through Christ, and love and delight to live according to God's will in all good works.
A temporary emotional high when experiencing God's blessings, which gradually fades as life's difficulties and challenges accumulate
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Heartfelt joy in God through Christ, and love and delight to live according to God's will in all good works.

options: Works that comply with church traditions and the teachings of learned religious leaders, even if Scripture seems to suggest otherwise
Works that accomplish much good in society and receive approval from communities, regardless of the religious motives behind them
Works that feel morally right to our conscience, whether or not they align with specific biblical commands or principles
Works from true faith, according to God's law, to His glory, not based on our opinions or human precepts.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Works from true faith, according to God's law, to His glory, not based on our opinions or human precepts.

options: The ceremonial laws of Moses regarding sacrifices, feasts, and temple worship.
The Ten Commandments of God revealed to Moses at Mount Sinai.
The laws of Christ summed up in the twofold command to love.
The civil laws of Israel for governing their kingdom and their nation.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: The Ten Commandments of God revealed to Moses at Mount Sinai.

options: Trust and obey the one God while maintaining loyalty to family, nation, and personal ambitions within reasonable limits always
Believe that God exists, avoid speaking His name irreverently, and acknowledge Him publicly without necessarily obeying all His commands
Acknowledge that God is supreme while respecting other religions' worship practices and integrating their wisdom into your personal faith
Flee idolatry; know, trust, and submit to the only God alone; love, fear, and honour Him with all heart; forsake all rather than disobey.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Flee idolatry; know, trust, and submit to the only God alone; love, fear, and honour Him with all heart; forsake all rather than disobey.

options: Refusing to worship any god because of doubt about God's existence or the reliability of Scripture's testimony about Him
Having or inventing something to trust in instead of or along with the only true God revealed in His Word.
Making carved statues or images to represent God for use in worship, which directly violates His command against graven idols
Worshipping God while also respecting the religious practices and deities honored by other cultures and nations as equally valid
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Having or inventing something to trust in instead of or along with the only true God revealed in His Word.

options: Images of any kind are prohibited absolutely, including images of creatures and saints, because all represent turning from God
Yes, we may make images of God for churches to help people understand divine nature and to aid in worship
We may make images of creatures but are forbidden from making any images whatsoever, since all image-making displeases God
No. God cannot be visibly portrayed. Creatures may be portrayed, but forbidden for worship or serving God through them.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. God cannot be visibly portrayed. Creatures may be portrayed, but forbidden for worship or serving God through them.

options: The church may use images for instruction, though preaching is also necessary.
Yes, images teach the unlettered laity more effectively than any preaching.
Images may be tolerated in churches but never worshipped or honoured.
No. God wants His people taught by living preaching of His Word, not by dumb images.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. God wants His people taught by living preaching of His Word, not by dumb images.

options: Three persons in the Godhead—Father, Son, Spirit—one God in essence and power
One divine person manifesting in three different roles—as Father in creation, Son in redemption, Spirit in sanctification of believers
The Father is God; the Son and Spirit are created beings subordinate to the Father's authority and power
Four distinct divine persons unified in authority, the Father, Son, Spirit, and a fourth divine principle or emanation
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: Three persons in the Godhead—Father, Son, Spirit—one God in essence and power

options: The universal congregation of all believers throughout history who have true faith, regardless of doctrine or practice
A social organization dedicated to moral improvement and community service in the name of Christian faith and ideals
An institution governed by church leaders whose traditions and teachings guide believers in their understanding of Scripture
The organized society of professing believers where the Gospel is truly preached and ordinances rightly administered
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: The organized society of professing believers where the Gospel is truly preached and ordinances rightly administered

options: We request God to provide only spiritual blessing while avoiding concern for physical food and daily necessities
We ask God to give us unlimited abundance and all material desires we seek throughout our lifetime
We petition God to grant us material success and pleasure as evidence of His favor toward us
We pray for a competent portion of life's good things and God's blessing
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: We pray for a competent portion of life's good things and God's blessing

options: We request that God forgive us our debts while we withhold forgiveness from those who owe us harm
We pray that God removes our guilt only after we demonstrate sufficient personal repentance and self-punishment for sins
We ask God to forgive us only if we first achieve perfect forgiveness toward all others who wronged us
We pray God would freely pardon our sins, encouraged because He enables us to forgive
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: We pray God would freely pardon our sins, encouraged because He enables us to forgive

options: We request protection from evil by depending entirely on our own moral strength and willpower to resist
We ask God to ensure we never experience any temptation, struggle, or difficulty in our Christian journey
We pray God would either keep us from temptation or support us when tempted
We pray that God removes all testing and difficulty from life, because temptation indicates His displeasure with us
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: We pray God would either keep us from temptation or support us when tempted

options: God's decrees are accomplished through human free will and choice
God executes His decrees only through the laws of nature
God's decrees are carried out by angels and spiritual beings alone
God executes His decrees in the works of creation and providence.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: God executes His decrees in the works of creation and providence.

options: God's making all things from nothing by the word of His power.
An eternal process of self-organization of pre-existing matter into visible forms.
The natural unfolding of divine potential through impersonal forces without direction.
God's arranging and organizing already-existing material over many ages of time.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: God's making all things from nothing by the word of His power.

options: As immortal spirits inhabiting material bodies without responsibility for the creation.
After the image of the angels and heavenly beings, though inferior in nature.
God created man male and female in His image, in knowledge and holiness.
In the divine image but later corrupted by Satan before completion.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: God created man male and female in His image, in knowledge and holiness.

options: God's setting the universe in motion and allowing natural laws to operate.
The universe operating entirely through chance and random events without divine direction.
God's most holy, wise, and powerful preserving and governing all creatures.
God's plan for a distant future but not involvement in daily affairs.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: God's most holy, wise, and powerful preserving and governing all creatures.

options: Unintentional error and weakness in attempting to follow moral law
Behavior that violates human moral standards and civil laws
Any want of conformity unto, or transgression of, God's law
Deliberate choice to break God's stated commands through willful sinful rebellion
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: Any want of conformity unto, or transgression of, God's law

options: To achieve happiness and success in all worldly pursuits
To serve mankind and build a perfect society on earth
To acquire knowledge and develop our natural talents and abilities
Man's chief end is to glorify God and to enjoy Him forever
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: Man's chief end is to glorify God and to enjoy Him forever

options: All mankind, descending from Adam, sinned in him and fell with him
All mankind chose to sin independently like Adam did
Only Adam sinned; the rest of mankind inherit the consequence
Only those who consciously choose to sin are held responsible
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: All mankind, descending from Adam, sinned in him and fell with him

options: Christ was born a normal human and later adopted into divine sonship when the Spirit descended at baptism
The eternal Christ-Spirit became human in Jesus while not truly possessing a body or suffering any human limitation
Christ took a true body and soul, conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of Mary
Christ took a human body from Mary but possessed a divine spirit rather than a human soul
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: Christ took a true body and soul, conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of Mary

options: An act of God's free grace whereby we are received as sons of God
A legal process where we earn the right to be God's children
A state we achieve through perfect obedience to God's law
The natural result of being born into a Christian family
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: An act of God's free grace whereby we are received as sons of God

options: God requires man's obedience to His revealed will
To strive to do whatever makes us happy and fulfilled
To obey the moral law we discover through our own reason
To follow the teachings of religious leaders and traditions
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: God requires man's obedience to His revealed will

options: A civil law for governing the ancient Jewish nation
The moral law God revealed to man for his obedience
The natural law written in man's conscience and reason
A ceremonial law to be observed in the tabernacle
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: The moral law God revealed to man for his obedience

options: The moral law is found in the ceremonial laws of the Old Testament
The moral law is summarized in the Sermon on the Mount
The moral law is summarily comprehended in the Ten Commandments.
The moral law is revealed through nature and human conscience alone
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: The moral law is summarily comprehended in the Ten Commandments.

options: The testimony of early church fathers alone confirms the Bible's authority
Scientific evidence and historical research prove the Bible is God's Word
We know the Bible is God's Word because it never contradicts itself
The Spirit of God bearing witness in our hearts persuades us the Bible is God's Word
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: The Spirit of God bearing witness in our hearts persuades us the Bible is God's Word

options: Thou shalt love God with all thy heart and serve Him alone above all else
Thou shalt not worship false gods or spiritual powers other than the Lord
Thou shalt have no graven images or likenesses of anything in heaven or on earth
The first commandment is, "Thou shalt have no other Gods before me."
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: The first commandment is, "Thou shalt have no other Gods before me."

options: An all-powerful being bound by time and subject to change like creation.
A Spirit, infinite, eternal, and unchangeable in His being, wisdom, power.
A finite deity with limitations in knowledge, power, or moral perfection.
A material being with a physical body in some location in space.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: A Spirit, infinite, eternal, and unchangeable in His being, wisdom, power.

options: To demonstrate that human effort and obedience can achieve the righteousness required by God
To show God's hatred of sinners and to condemn unbelievers to eternal punishment
To reveal God's perfect righteousness so His people know His will and ungodly are convicted
To prepare people for salvation by removing sins through perfect obedience to God's commands
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: To reveal God's perfect righteousness so His people know His will and ungodly are convicted

options: Some sins, by reason of aggravations, are more heinous in God's sight
The severity of sin depends entirely on how we feel about it
Sins against men are more serious than sins against God
All sins are equally sinful and deserve the same punishment
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: Some sins, by reason of aggravations, are more heinous in God's sight

options: A saving grace whereby we receive and rest upon Christ alone for salvation
Belief in Christian doctrine and intellectual agreement that Jesus died for human sins
Commitment to moral self-improvement and personal effort to live according to biblical principles
Trust in religious works and sacraments through the church for eternal life and salvation
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: A saving grace whereby we receive and rest upon Christ alone for salvation

options: Established by church councils as tests of faith and loyalty to Christian authority
Commanded by God in the Old Testament as signs of judgment for sin
Created by church tradition to symbolize spiritual truths without conferring any real grace to believers
Specially instituted by Christ to represent and apply to believers benefits of the new covenant
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: Specially instituted by Christ to represent and apply to believers benefits of the new covenant

options: Thou shalt not swear by God's name falsely or make rash oaths that thou intendest later to break
Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; the Lord will not hold him guiltless
Thou shalt keep all thy vows made unto the Lord and not speak profanely or irreverently of His holy name
Thou shalt always speak reverently of God and avoid all forms of profanity, blasphemy, and irreverent speech toward Him
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:puritan_.answer_choice: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; the Lord will not hold him guiltless

options: Infants should be baptized as members of Christian families in obedience to church tradition
No; infants are not to be baptized; there is neither command nor example in Scripture
Children must be baptized to receive saving grace, since baptism removes original sin
Yes, infants may be baptized because they inherit the covenant through believing parents
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:puritan_.answer_choice: No; infants are not to be baptized; there is neither command nor example in Scripture

options: The Father begets the Son, the Son is begotten of the Father, and the Holy Ghost proceeds from both eternally.
The Father is almighty and eternal, the Son is our Redeemer and mediator, and the Holy Spirit is our comforter and guide.
The Father made the heavens and earth, the Son became incarnate and died for our sins, and the Spirit sanctifies believers.
The Father is the source of all things, the Son reveals the Father's will, and the Spirit applies redemption to believers.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: The Father begets the Son, the Son is begotten of the Father, and the Holy Ghost proceeds from both eternally.

options: Only the preface and reasons of the Ten Commandments require consideration, not their substance
The substance of the commandments is the only thing to consider; the preface and reasons are less important
Consider the preface, substance of the commandments, and reasons annexed to some to enforce them
The commandments have no particular preface or annexed reasons, but stand as bare commands from God
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Consider the preface, substance of the commandments, and reasons annexed to some to enforce them

options: The sum of our duty to God is to perfectly obey the Ten Commandments and keep all his statutes
To fear God's wrath, obey his law, and trust only in his provision for our lives
Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, strength, and mind
To love God with all our might and to perform all the works that demonstrate this love
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, strength, and mind

options: Atheism and the denial of God, idolatry, swearing false oaths, murder, theft, adultery, dishonoring parents, lying, and perjury
Atheism and denial of God's existence, idolatry, swearing falsely by God's name, murder, theft, adultery, disrespecting parents, and perjury
Atheism, idolatry, swearing falsely by God's name, murder, theft, adultery, dishonoring parents, bearing false witness, and coveting possessions
Atheism, idolatry, omission of duties, ignorance, false thoughts of God, profaneness, hatred, self-love, inordinate affections, unbelief, despair, hardness, pride, tempting God
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Atheism, idolatry, omission of duties, ignorance, false thoughts of God, profaneness, hatred, self-love, inordinate affections, unbelief, despair, hardness, pride, tempting God

options: The sabbath is primarily for the common people; superiors need only ensure legal observance
Directed to governors and superiors; they must keep it and ensure those under them observe it and not hinder them
The sabbath command applies equally to all people without any special charge to superiors and governors
Governors and superiors are exempt from keeping the sabbath so they can oversee their responsibilities
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Directed to governors and superiors; they must keep it and ensure those under them observe it and not hinder them

options: Remembering the Sabbath means taking time for rest alone, without concern for spiritual worship or creation's significance
The word Remember is included to remind us that the Sabbath was created for human convenience and leisure
Remembering helps in preparation and keeping it, recalls creation and redemption, comes once weekly amid competing worldly cares and cares
The fourth commandment requires God's people to work six days with one day of rest in complete idleness
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Remembering helps in preparation and keeping it, recalls creation and redemption, comes once weekly amid competing worldly cares and cares

options: To rule over your neighbor wisely and ensure they fulfill their obligations to you
Love your neighbor as yourself, and do to others as you would have them do to you
The sum of duty to man is to seek your own good first and help others when convenient
To maintain justice and equality by giving others what they earn through their own efforts
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Love your neighbor as yourself, and do to others as you would have them do to you

options: Spiritual leaders and pastors exclusively, since the church is God's institution for directing believers' lives and growth
Political rulers and civic authorities alone, who govern the commonwealth and deserve honor as representatives of God
Not only natural parents, but all superiors in age and gifts, especially those in authority in family, church, commonwealth
Only biological parents, since the commandment specifically uses the word 'father' and 'mother' literally in each case
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Not only natural parents, but all superiors in age and gifts, especially those in authority in family, church, commonwealth

options: Styled Father and Mother to teach superiors to be like parents expressing love and tenderness, making inferiors more willing in duties
Styled Father and Mother merely as traditional honorary titles honoring ancient custom, without implying loving care or concern
Called Father and Mother to reflect their absolute authority and power, similar to how strict parents govern children
Named Father and Mother because superiors must exercise firm discipline and correction over inferiors, like fathers discipline children
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Styled Father and Mother to teach superiors to be like parents expressing love and tenderness, making inferiors more willing in duties

options: God elected all people to salvation through Christ and earnestly desires that none should perish but all be saved.
God has eternally elected some angels to glory and some men to eternal life in Christ, and foreordained others to wrath.
God chose some to be His covenant people based on His foreknowledge of their goodness and righteousness.
God foresaw who would believe in Christ and predestined only those who exercise faith to salvation and eternal life.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: God has eternally elected some angels to glory and some men to eternal life in Christ, and foreordained others to wrath.

options: Attempting to reform subordinates' personal character beyond their calling and role, extending authority improperly into family and personal private affairs
Neglect of duties, seeking own glory and pleasure, commanding unlawful things, counseling in evil, dissuading from good, unduly correcting, exposing to danger
Overexercising power and authority beyond lawful limits, denying subordinates any freedom of personal conscience, and demanding their complete obedience
Any failure whatsoever to enforce established laws and rules, showing unwarranted mercy when discipline is deserved, and refusing to correct subordinates
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Neglect of duties, seeking own glory and pleasure, commanding unlawful things, counseling in evil, dissuading from good, unduly correcting, exposing to danger

options: Regard each other's dignity and worth, give honor, and rejoice in each other's gifts and advancement
To subordinate yourself to whichever equal seems most worthy at any given time
To maintain strict equality by never allowing anyone to receive greater honor or advancement
To compete with one another for recognition and to advance your own gifts above others
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Regard each other's dignity and worth, give honor, and rejoice in each other's gifts and advancement

options: Honoring one person more than others, preferring certain friendships above other relationships within the community
Celebrating others' success, acknowledging their talents, and supporting their advancement in various areas of life
Respecting authority figures and accepting their leadership role within the church and social structure
Neglect of duties, undervaluing worth, envying gifts, grieving at advancement and prosperity, usurping preeminence
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Neglect of duties, undervaluing worth, envying gifts, grieving at advancement and prosperity, usurping preeminence

options: Taking life is completely forbidden in all circumstances whatsoever, including lawful public justice, defensive warfare, and self-defense against attackers
Killing is prohibited except when motivated by personal anger and revenge, and when defending one's own honor and reputation
Murder is forbidden, but sinful anger toward wrongdoers, quarreling with rivals, harsh words, and striking in self-defense are permitted
Taking life except public justice, war, or defense; sinful anger, hatred, envy, revenge; immoderate use; provoking words; oppression; quarreling; striking
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Taking life except public justice, war, or defense; sinful anger, hatred, envy, revenge; immoderate use; provoking words; oppression; quarreling; striking

options: The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt not steal.
The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt not bear false witness.
The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt honor thy father and mother.
The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt not commit adultery.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt not steal.

options: Not all permitted to read publicly; all bound to read privately with families; scriptures translated to vulgar languages
All people are permitted and encouraged to read God's word publicly in the congregation without restriction
Only trained ministers and church leaders should read Scripture, not common people in their homes
The word should remain only in original languages so people depend on authorized interpreters
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Not all permitted to read publicly; all bound to read privately with families; scriptures translated to vulgar languages

options: With reverent esteem, firm persuasion they are God's word, desire to obey, diligence, attention, meditation, application, self-denial, and prayer
Quickly skimming Scripture to find isolated verses supporting one's existing beliefs and opinions without careful study
By casual reading without much reflection, accepting church teachings as equally authoritative as the biblical text itself
Privately reading Scripture while skeptical of its authority, trusting personal interpretation over scholarly and church tradition
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: With reverent esteem, firm persuasion they are God's word, desire to obey, diligence, attention, meditation, application, self-denial, and prayer

options: Any believer with zeal for God may preach the word publicly without formal approval
The word should be preached by all who have good intentions and moral character
Preaching requires only approval from the local congregation, not genuine spiritual gifts
Only by those sufficiently gifted, duly approved, and called to the office of preaching
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Only by those sufficiently gifted, duly approved, and called to the office of preaching

options: God created angels as immortal, holy spirits of knowledge and power, to execute commandments and praise God, yet subject to change.
God fashioned the angels from the dust of the earth as He did man, but gave them spiritual bodies.
God caused the angels to evolve from lower creatures over time, perfecting them into spiritual beings of great power.
God created angels as pure spirits composed of divine substance, eternal and unchangeable like God Himself.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: God created angels as immortal, holy spirits of knowledge and power, to execute commandments and praise God, yet subject to change.

options: Sacraments administered automatically convey grace to anyone who participates, regardless of faith or covenant status
A sacrament is a human institution designed to teach morality and good behavior
A sacrament is merely a symbolic ritual without true spiritual significance or connection to Christ's mediation
Holy ordinance instituted by Christ to signify, seal, and exhibit benefits of his mediation to those in covenant of grace
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Holy ordinance instituted by Christ to signify, seal, and exhibit benefits of his mediation to those in covenant of grace

options: The inward grace is what matters; the outward sign is arbitrary and could be changed
The parts of sacraments vary; some have only outward signs and others only inward grace
Only the outward sign matters in a sacrament; the spiritual grace is entirely dependent on the recipient's faith
Two parts: an outward sensible sign according to Christ's appointment, and an inward spiritual grace signified thereby
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Two parts: an outward sensible sign according to Christ's appointment, and an inward spiritual grace signified thereby

options: Receiving baptism once and forgetting it, assuming all subsequent sins are automatically covered forever
Serious and thankful consideration of baptism's nature, benefits, and vow; humbling for sin; assurance of pardon; drawing strength from Christ's death
Relying solely on baptism for salvation without need to grow in faith or live righteously
Viewing baptism merely as a social ritual joining the church, with little spiritual regard
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Serious and thankful consideration of baptism's nature, benefits, and vow; humbling for sin; assurance of pardon; drawing strength from Christ's death

options: Ministers set apart bread and wine by word of institution, thanksgiving, and prayer; give to communicants who eat and drink
The priest consecrates bread and wine, magically changing their substance into Christ's body and blood
Bread and wine remain only symbols with no special treatment, distributed like ordinary food to church members
The blessing transforms elements into Christ's literal body through the power of consecration formula
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Ministers set apart bread and wine by word of institution, thanksgiving, and prayer; give to communicants who eat and drink

options: Those unsure of faith should wait until achieving perfect certainty of belief before approaching the communion table
Anyone doubting their salvation is automatically unfit for communion and should be refused the sacrament by church leaders
People uncertain of their conversion should abstain from communion until achieving complete and perfect certainty of grace
May have true interest if affected by lack and unfeignedly desires Christ; sacrament for weak and doubting; should come for strengthening
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: May have true interest if affected by lack and unfeignedly desires Christ; sacrament for weak and doubting; should come for strengthening

options: Both authored by God; spiritual part is Christ and his benefits; seals of same covenant; dispensed by gospel ministers only
Both sacraments are optional ceremonies that may be dispensed by any faithful believer
Baptism and the Supper are different in their authors, spiritual meanings, and how they should be administered
The sacraments were instituted by the apostles as Church traditions and will end with the current age
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Both authored by God; spiritual part is Christ and his benefits; seals of same covenant; dispensed by gospel ministers only

options: Baptism administered once with water for regeneration; Lord's supper administered often with bread and wine for spiritual nourishment
Both baptism and Lord's supper administered once with water and bread as signs and seals of faith
Baptism administered often with water for regeneration; Lord's supper administered once with bread and wine for nourishment
Baptism with bread and wine for regeneration; Lord's supper with water for spiritual nourishment of believers
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Baptism administered once with water for regeneration; Lord's supper administered often with bread and wine for spiritual nourishment

options: Saints and angels hear requests and pardon sins; prayer may be made to them for intercession
God, magistrates, and ministers can hear prayer; prayer is to be made to all of them
God only can search hearts, hear requests, and pardon sins; prayer is to be made to him alone
God and deceased saints hear prayer; they should be prayed to for their intercession with God
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: God only can search hearts, hear requests, and pardon sins; prayer is to be made to him alone

options: The Old Testament law required it; covenant promises depend on using Christ's name in all our prayers
Man's sinfulness and distance from God make Christ alone the appointed mediator; we must pray in his name
The Spirit commands it in Scripture; apostles taught it as the primary way to approach God in prayer
Mary, the mother of Jesus, intercedes for us as the great mediator between God and all sinners
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Man's sinfulness and distance from God make Christ alone the appointed mediator; we must pray in his name

options: Spirit teaches only the elect and learned how to pray; common people must rely on ministers
Spirit helps by enabling understanding of for whom, what, and how to pray; works requisite graces in our hearts
Spirit prevents sinful thoughts and makes prayer unnecessary through constant intervention; helps only the ordained clergy pray
Spirit writes down prayers and presents them to God; only ministers' prayers receive God's full attention
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Spirit helps by enabling understanding of for whom, what, and how to pray; works requisite graces in our hearts

options: Ourselves and our friends only; prayers for others are presumptuous and beyond our proper Christian concern
Magistrates and ministers only, as they are appointed by God to receive our petitions and prayers
Whole church, magistrates, ministers, ourselves, brethren, enemies, and all men living or to come; but not the dead
All men, living, dead, and yet to be born, including those who have sinned the sin unto death
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Whole church, magistrates, ministers, ourselves, brethren, enemies, and all men living or to come; but not the dead

options: All things tending to God's glory, the church's welfare, our own or others' good; but not unlawful things
Only spiritual blessings and matters of soul; material needs and worldly prosperity are not proper prayer requests
God's glory alone, never our own welfare or others', as such prayer would be selfish and wrong
Anything we desire and request, whether lawful or unlawful, as God judges all petitions impartially
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: All things tending to God's glory, the church's welfare, our own or others' good; but not unlawful things

options: By pouring out complaints and demands, expecting God to grant wishes without gratitude or respect for His sovereign will
By making vows to God that one intends to break, and negotiating with God for personal benefit alone
Casually mentioning requests to God while focusing mainly on worldly concerns and temporal pleasures of life
With apprehension of God's majesty, sense of unworthiness, penitent and thankful hearts, understanding, faith, sincerity, fervency, love, and perseverance
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: With apprehension of God's majesty, sense of unworthiness, penitent and thankful hearts, understanding, faith, sincerity, fervency, love, and perseverance

options: Primarily as an expression of Christian identity, more important for memorization than for actual prayer practice
Only as a pattern to learn from, never to be used directly as a prayer in worship services
As a magical formula believed to guarantee answered prayers when recited with sufficient emotional intensity and frequency
As pattern for other prayers and as prayer itself, with understanding, faith, reverence, and other necessary graces
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: As pattern for other prayers and as prayer itself, with understanding, faith, reverence, and other necessary graces

options: Four parts: preface, petitions, doxology, and conclusion
Three parts: a preface, petitions, and a conclusion
Seven parts distributed throughout the prayer in theological order
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Three parts: a preface, petitions, and a conclusion

options: God permitted all angels to fall willfully into sin and damnation; He employs them to bring glory to Satan.
God permitted some angels to fall willfully into sin and damnation; He established the rest in holiness and employs both to His glory.
God prevented some angels from falling into sin and damnation; the rest fell and are employed in judgment.
God permitted some angels to fall through temptation and weakness; He established the rest but employs some unwillingly.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: God permitted some angels to fall willfully into sin and damnation; He established the rest in holiness and employs both to His glory.

options: Everlasting weeping and gnashing of teeth, torments of the lake of fire, but with periods of rest.
Everlasting separation from God's comfortable presence but without torment, dwelling in outer darkness forever in solitude.
Everlasting separation from God's comfortable presence and most grievous torments in soul and body, without intermission, in hell fire forever.
Temporary separation from God's presence and moderate torments in soul and body, then eventual restoration to fellowship.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Everlasting separation from God's comfortable presence and most grievous torments in soul and body, without intermission, in hell fire forever.

options: The covenant of grace was made with Abraham and his descendants; it was renewed with the people of Israel.
The covenant of grace was made with Christ as the second Adam, and in him with all the elect as his seed.
The covenant of grace was made with all believers who trust in Jesus Christ as their personal Savior.
The covenant of grace was made with all humanity; God offers salvation freely to anyone who will accept it.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: The covenant of grace was made with Christ as the second Adam, and in him with all the elect as his seed.

options: God gives His Holy Spirit only to those who work righteousness and demonstrate faith through good deeds.
God provides a Mediator; believers must work to receive faith through their own efforts and holy obedience.
God freely provides salvation through promises; believers must receive faith and achieve holiness through moral discipline.
God freely provides a Mediator and life and salvation by Him; He gives His Holy Spirit to work faith in believers and enable holy obedience.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: God freely provides a Mediator and life and salvation by Him; He gives His Holy Spirit to work faith in believers and enable holy obedience.

options: The covenant of grace was not always administered the same way; Old Testament administrations differed from New Testament administrations.
The Old Testament knew nothing of grace; it was purely law until the New Testament brought grace.
The covenant of grace was always administered the same way in both Old and New Testament eras.
The covenant of grace was administered only in the New Testament; the Old Testament had no covenant grace.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: The covenant of grace was not always administered the same way; Old Testament administrations differed from New Testament administrations.

options: By promises, prophecies, sacrifices, circumcision, passover, and types which foresignified Christ to come; sufficient to give full remission of sins and eternal salvation.
By the law, temple sacrifices, and priestly mediation; sufficient to reveal God's will but not provide full remission.
By ceremonial laws, the priesthood, and the tabernacle structure; sufficient preparation for the coming Messiah's work.
By prophetic promises and the passover feast alone; insufficient without the New Testament sacraments for salvation.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: By promises, prophecies, sacrifices, circumcision, passover, and types which foresignified Christ to come; sufficient to give full remission of sins and eternal salvation.

options: By the priesthood and private confession; grace held forth exclusively to baptized members of the visible church.
By the five sacraments and apostolic tradition; grace held forth in equal measure as the Old Testament.
By preaching and administering extreme unction and confirmation; grace held forth in complete evidence to all believers.
By preaching the Word and administering Baptism and Lord's Supper; grace and salvation are held forth in fuller evidence and efficacy to all nations.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: By preaching the Word and administering Baptism and Lord's Supper; grace and salvation are held forth in fuller evidence and efficacy to all nations.

options: The church and its ordained ministers, who stand as mediators between God and individual believers in hearing confessions.
Moses and the prophets, through whom God mediated His covenant to the Old Testament people of Israel.
The Holy Spirit, who applies the grace of Christ to believers and mediates between God and the church through spiritual gifts.
The Lord Jesus Christ, eternal Son of God, equal with the Father, is the sole Mediator of the covenant of grace.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: The Lord Jesus Christ, eternal Son of God, equal with the Father, is the sole Mediator of the covenant of grace.

options: Our Mediator was called Jesus, because he is our Lord and King who rules over all nations.
Our Mediator was called Jesus, because he taught His disciples the way to eternal life and righteousness.
Our Mediator was called Jesus, because he saveth his people from their sins.
Our Mediator was called Jesus, because he heals the sick and performs mighty works and miracles.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Our Mediator was called Jesus, because he saveth his people from their sins.

options: His exalted state wherein Christ is advanced to the highest favor with God, possessing all power and glory in heaven and earth.
His miracles and mighty works by which He demonstrated His divine power and authority over sickness, demons, and nature.
That low condition wherein Christ, emptying Himself of glory, took the form of a servant from conception through death until resurrection.
His role as prophet, priest, and king, in which He teaches God's will, offers Himself as sacrifice, and rules creation.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: That low condition wherein Christ, emptying Himself of glory, took the form of a servant from conception through death until resurrection.

options: From eternity the Son of God in Father's bosom, He became son of man, made of a woman of low estate, born in abasement.
Born miraculously without human father; He was recognized by kings and shepherds as the great King of Israel.
Born to Mary, a righteous and faithful woman; He was blessed above all births and honored by all who saw Him.
Born during Caesar Augustus' reign; His birth brought great joy to Jerusalem and was welcomed by the Jewish leaders.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: From eternity the Son of God in Father's bosom, He became son of man, made of a woman of low estate, born in abasement.

options: By fulfilling only the ceremonial law; by enduring worldly suffering, demonic opposition, and natural human limitations.
By exempting Himself from the law's requirements and displaying divine power; by conquering worldly indignities without temptation.
By subjecting Himself to the law and perfectly fulfilling it; by conflicting with the world's indignities, Satan's temptations, and human infirmities.
By demonstrating perfect obedience to tradition and society; by avoiding Satan's temptations and remaining separate from human weakness.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: By subjecting Himself to the law and perfectly fulfilling it; by conflicting with the world's indignities, Satan's temptations, and human infirmities.

options: Betrayed, forsaken, rejected, condemned; He endured wrath, terrors of death and darkness, laid down His life as offering for sin on shameful cursed cross.
Betrayed by Peter, rejected by Jews, condemned by Herod; endured physical suffering on the cross before resurrection.
Betrayed by His disciples, forsaken by God, condemned to eternal separation; died as a martyr's example.
Abandoned by apostles, condemned by the people, endured death fearfully; the wrath of God was withheld.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Betrayed, forsaken, rejected, condemned; He endured wrath, terrors of death and darkness, laid down His life as offering for sin on shameful cursed cross.

options: Christ was buried by His disciples and remained in Hades until God raised Him on the third day.
Christ's body was laid in a tomb and His soul went to paradise; He was not truly dead but sleeping.
Christ was buried and remained under death's power for three days; expressed as 'He descended into hell.'
Christ's humiliation ended at death; after death He entered glory and ceased to suffer for mankind.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Christ was buried and remained under death's power for three days; expressed as 'He descended into hell.'

options: Rose without the same physical body; proclaimed Himself God's Son, ended Satan's reign, established the law.
Rose with a spiritual body only; demonstrated His power, defeated sin, and became Lord of the apostles.
He rose with His same body without corruption; He declared Himself God's Son, satisfied divine justice, vanquished death, and became Head of His Church.
Rose with immortal body free from weakness; revealed His divinity, satisfied the law, ascended to heaven.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: He rose with His same body without corruption; He declared Himself God's Son, satisfied divine justice, vanquished death, and became Head of His Church.

options: After forty days appearing and commissioning apostles to preach, He visibly ascended to highest heavens as our head, triumphing to prepare a place for us.
After fifty days appearing and choosing apostles, ascended to sit at God's right hand preparing judgment.
Appearing to apostles for many days before ascending, He triumphed over enemies and prepared His throne.
After three days appearing to disciples, ascended spiritually to heaven without visible departure, promising the Comforter.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: After forty days appearing and commissioning apostles to preach, He visibly ascended to highest heavens as our head, triumphing to prepare a place for us.

options: Christ rules only over the invisible church in heaven, having no authority or involvement with earthly matters and governments.
Christ waits passively in heaven until the day of judgment, performing no active work on behalf of His people.
Christ at God's right hand has full power and glory, defends His church, furnishes gifts and graces, and intercedes for us.
Christ continues in His humiliation, hiding His glory and submitting to the rule of earthly powers and Satan.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Christ at God's right hand has full power and glory, defends His church, furnishes gifts and graces, and intercedes for us.

options: By appearing before Father in our nature, presenting His merit and sacrifice, declaring their application to believers, answering accusations before God's throne.
By praying for believers in heaven, presenting their faith and obedience, interceding with God for their acceptance and protection.
By sitting at God's right hand, judging the works of believers, presenting their righteousness, and answering Satan's charges.
By appearing before God's throne in divine glory, presenting the law fulfilled, applying grace to all nations worldwide.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: By appearing before Father in our nature, presenting His merit and sacrifice, declaring their application to believers, answering accusations before God's throne.

options: Christ shall return only in the hearts of believers through the work of the Holy Spirit, not in bodily form.
Christ shall come in humility and meekness, not in power and glory, to call all people to repentance and faith.
Christ shall come secretly and invisibly to rapture His church away before the world's destruction and final judgment.
Christ shall come at the last day in great power and glory, with His holy angels, to judge the world in righteousness.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Christ shall come at the last day in great power and glory, with His holy angels, to judge the world in righteousness.

options: Christ by His obedience procured righteousness for believers; His sacrifice removed all punishment from those who trust in Him.
Christ by His death procured forgiveness for believers; His resurrection ensures that all will eventually reach heaven.
Christ by His teaching procured wisdom for believers; His example shows us the way to eternal life and happiness.
Christ, by his mediation, hath procured redemption, with all other benefits of the covenant of grace.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Christ, by his mediation, hath procured redemption, with all other benefits of the covenant of grace.

options: Those who faithfully keep the moral law, produce good works, and demonstrate their worthiness through righteous living.
All people universally, since Christ's redemption is offered to all and none are excluded from the possibility of salvation.
Only those who are predestined from the foundation of the world and who never fall away from the faith.
Those for whom Christ purchased redemption, who by the Holy Ghost are enabled to believe in Christ according to the gospel.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Those for whom Christ purchased redemption, who by the Holy Ghost are enabled to believe in Christ according to the gospel.

options: The scriptures make known what God requires of us, how He forgave all sins, and how we should live.
The scriptures make known what God is, the persons in the Godhead, his decrees, and the execution of his decrees.
The scriptures make known God's love for mankind, the history of Israel, and predictions about the future.
The scriptures make known God's laws and commandments, the stories of the prophets, and lives of the apostles.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: The scriptures make known what God is, the persons in the Godhead, his decrees, and the execution of his decrees.

options: Enjoys ecclesiastical power, temporal blessing, spiritual fellowship; communion of saints in visible unity, salvation for believers only.
